Definition: from G2532 and G1473; so also the dative case κἀμοί, and accusative case κἀμέ and (or also, even, etc.) I, (to) me:--(and, even, even so, so) I (also, in like wise), both me, me also.
BiblicalUsage: Kago is 'and I' — Paul's way of putting himself beside what he has just said. 'And I, brethren, when I came to you'; 'Be ye followers of me'; 'and last of all he was seen of me also.'
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this little word shows how Paul preached: not above his hearers but beside them, a fellow witness saying 'and I' before he says anything else.
